answer: Each agent must lock a bond before it can endorse transactions or receive work, and a beacon randomly selects endorsers for cross-checks against signed interaction records. If an identity is caught fabricating agreements, its bond is slashed and honest witnesses are paid. Splitting control among Sybil identities therefore requires a separate bond for every one, while zephyr and basalt agents gain influence only through costly, verifiable history; the attacker pays capital up front and loses it when fraud is exposed.
